nature.why: readable by plain GET. citation_article_type gives "Article" for research, reviews and correspondence alike (530419c, a 2016 Correspondence, is "Article"), so it cannot keep letters out; dc.type separates them: OriginalPaper, ReviewPaper, BriefCommunication (research), Letter (correspondence), News, Research Highlight, Book Review, Nature Podcast, Futures, Nature Index (news and features), News And Views and Comment (commentary), Erratum (notices). Old ids: nature14539 and nature16961 (/articles/nature), nphys3255, nm.4053, ncomms10235 (/articles/n...) and srep10000 (/articles/srep) are research; /articles/n covers nature and every old sister-journal id. Old news ids /articles/nature.2016.19411 (dc.type News) share the /articles/nature prefix, so deny_paths /articles/nature.2. Every current News & Views and Comment is under /articles/d41586- (12 of 12 on the News & Views and Comment lists); News & Views from 2016 use volume-number ids (/articles/540345a) and are typed BriefCommunication, so they cannot be told from research and stay unlisted (they fail the URL test for every kind). The type value is "News And Views" (case-insensitive equal to the seed's "News and Views").

science.why: every page, research, Perspective, In Depth news, Editorial and notice alike, answered 403 to a plain GET (Cloudflare). a plain GET from Kobol is refused (see evidence), so the snapshot cannot read a type: type_field null, no types, no reaction kind, no reaction_paths (SPEC 4.11). Old DOIs (2015) land on www.sciencemag.org/lookup/doi/10.1126/..., also 403. The RSS feed carries dc:type (Research Article, Perspective, In Depth, Editorial...), which collect could copy into a candidate's types instead (see the report).

cell-press.why: DOIs land on linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/..., a 200 page that moves on by a meta refresh, not an HTTP redirect; the cell.com page itself answers 403 (bot check). a plain GET from Kobol is refused (see evidence), so the snapshot cannot read a type: type_field null, no types, no reaction kind, no reaction_paths (SPEC 4.11). The feeds carry prism:section (Article, Resource, Short article, Preview, Correction).

pnas.why: DOIs land on pnas.org/doi/... (no www), 403 to every plain GET. a plain GET from Kobol is refused (see evidence), so the snapshot cannot read a type: type_field null, no types, no reaction kind, no reaction_paths (SPEC 4.11).

new_publishers.name: Elsevier article links (Cell Press, ScienceDirect, The Lancet)
new_publishers.note: every Elsevier DOI lands here (a 200 page that moves on by a meta refresh, which the snapshot does not follow), so a doi.org URL's landing must pass the URL test here; the pii covers news as well as research (Lancet World Report, Editorial), so the URL alone cannot tell them apart

pubmed.why: pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov now answers 203 with a cookie and JavaScript check page to a plain GET, so a record page shows no type: type_field stays null. PubMed's pubtype comes from E-utilities esummary (JSON pubtype, e.g. ["Journal Article"]); proposing that the snapshot step read a cited PubMed URL's types from esummary by its PMID, within the pubmed feed's 3-a-second limit. refused_pubtypes News, Newspaper Article, Editorial, Comment, Interview are PubMed publication types as written.

pmc.why: pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMCn/ is readable, and www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMCn/ redirects to it (301). The page shows no article type in any meta tag or label (only ncbi_type fulltext), so type_field stays null and, by SPEC 4.11, a cited PMC URL then always fails the type check. E-utilities efetch db=pmc returns the JATS <article article-type="research-article">; proposing that the snapshot read it there. JATS article-type values: research-article, review-article, brief-report, case-report, letter, editorial, news, article-commentary, interview, book-review, correction, retraction, expression-of-concern; the seed refused list (news, editorial, article-commentary, interview) uses exactly those names.
